company_summary: The supplied snapshots contain almost no About Us narrative: from 2016 to 2024 the captured text is dominated by navigation menus, store contact details, and product/site-map listings, so stated-values language (e.g., 'Apple Values', 'Environment', 'Privacy', 'Inclusion and Diversity') appears only as menu labels rather than prose. The trajectory visible is primarily a shift in the navigation footprint: from a 2016 contact-and-jobs page, to a 2018 expansive product-catalogue menu including values-related links, to a slimmer 2020-2024 site map centred on product categories and services, with 'Apple Vision Pro' added in 2024 and 'Entertainment' and 'Apple Wallet' replacing 'Only on Apple' and 'Digital Wallet' in 2023. Any conclusions about stated values should be drawn from full page text rather than these extracts.

AbbVie's About Us language moved from an early patient-centered innovation framing (2016) and a stable 2017–2019 'research-driven biopharmaceutical' and 'Our Mission Hasn't Wavered' emphasis, to a sparser 2020–2022 focus on future possibility and 'unwavering commitment' with 'health of humankind' language. The 2023 page added explicit values language (diverse backgrounds, dignity and respect, highest standards in quality and compliance) and sustainability framing. By 2024 the page centred on 'who we are', with explicit values of compassion, innovation, inclusion, community service and integrity, and a restated mission to 'discover and deliver innovative medicines'.

Abbott's About Us page moved from an early 2016 framing of 'fulfilling the promise of human potential' and sustainability-oriented 'innovative, responsible and sustainable business' language toward a 2017-2018 'business of life' and 'anthem' framing centered on living fully. From 2020 onward the page settled on a product-and-purpose frame ('life-changing technology', 'our purpose is to make the world a better place') built around specific diagnostic and device examples, with the 'purpose' wording and technology emphasis then held stable through 2024. Across the period the page shrank from broad corporate-values rhetoric to a shorter, technology-centric statement with little explicit stakeholder or sustainability language after 2016.

Amazon's About Us-style pages moved from a 2016 baseline dominated by navigation and Prime promotion toward a richer narrative of 'builders', 'inventing on behalf of customers', and employee stories. From 2018 onward, sustainability, community investment and job creation became recurring themes, and in 2020 the page explicitly stated four guiding principles and a net zero shipment vision. By 2023 and 2024 the emphasis shifted toward AI, innovation, employee pay and inclusion, though the 2022 and 2024 snapshots are largely unpopulated templates, limiting direct comparison.

Broadcom's About Us language moved from a 2016 framing centred on semiconductor design, consumer-facing connectivity ('Connecting everything', 'Consumers might never see Broadcom's products') and engineering headcount, to a 2019 corporate framing as a 'global infrastructure technology leader' built on heritage from merged companies and adding 'infrastructure software' alongside semiconductors. The 2019 text is more abstract and enterprise-oriented, emphasising scale, portfolio diversity, and customers' business success rather than product stories. Only two snapshots are provided, so the trajectory beyond 2019 cannot be assessed from this material.

The snapshots show American Express's About Us language moving from a navigation-heavy product menu in 2016-2018 (promotional taglines like 'Great Escapes Start Here' and 'Always the right gift') to a structured corporate statement in 2019-2020 built around a Vision, Mission and six Values. The later framing centres on customer experience, aspiration and inclusion ('We Respect People', 'We Need Different Views', 'We Care About Communities'). Across the period the text emphasises customers and team rather than shareholders, and the 2019 and 2020 pages are identical, so the trajectory is one of a single structural shift followed by stability.

Bank of America's About Us page moved from a 2016 baseline built on veteran-employee testimonials and hiring commitments, through a 2017-2018 emphasis on housing, Yoobi, and disability inclusion, to 2021's explicit stakeholder-capitalism and racial-equality framing with a $1 billion commitment. From 2023 the page shifted to shorter, more general language about 'strengthening our communities', a 'diverse and inclusive workplace', and awards, with 2024 focusing on client, teammate and entrepreneur themes and little climate or stakeholder vocabulary. No 2022 snapshot was provided, so the 2023 note compares against 2021.

BlackRock's About Us language moves from a 2016-2018 baseline centred on world-class capabilities, a 'singular focus' on out-performing competitors, and responsibility framed around clients and philanthropy, toward a purpose-led framing of 'helping more and more people experience financial well-being' from 2019 onward. Sustainability and ESG vocabulary becomes embedded from 2018-2020, and the 2022-2024 pages adopt a 'bigger questions' narrative tied to net zero, inclusion, and stakeholders. Across the period the text shifts from a product and performance orientation to a stakeholder and societal-purpose orientation, with a long-running focus on retail investor access.

BMS's About Us language moved from a shareholder- and performance-forward BioPharma pitch in 2016 (total shareholder return, 300+ consecutive dividend quarters, 'BioPharma leader') toward a patient-centred, mission-led framing by 2021 ('mission is to discover, develop and deliver innovative medicines that help patients prevail over serious diseases'). Shareholder metrics disappeared after 2016, and values language ('Passion, innovation, urgency, accountability, inclusion and integrity') and 'health equity' appeared from 2020 onward. The 2024 version is largely stable, adding structured sections on ethics, inclusion and diversity, sustainability and responsibility.

The snapshots contain only the berkshirehathaway.com homepage and footer, not an About Us page, so no mission, values, or stakeholder language is available to analyse. Across 2016 to 2024 the text is nearly static: a GEICO insurance promotion, the corporate address, and a contact paragraph. The only substantive textual change is the removal of the email contact option after 2016, and the rest of the changes are copyright-year updates and one formatting change. The corpus therefore shows no observable shift in stated corporate values over this period.

Across the two available snapshots (2023 and 2024), Citigroup's About Us copy is largely stable. It frames Citi as a global bank for a complex, digitally driven world, with a mission of serving as a trusted partner to clients and quantified claims on flows, clients, ESG commitments and customers. The main change in 2024 is structural and presentational: a new headline, a bulleted layout, an explicit 'Our Mission' label, and added navigation to 'Our Businesses' and 'Citi Infographics'. Because only two snapshots were provided, this summary cannot describe the longer 2016 to 2024 trajectory.

ConocoPhillips' About Us language is largely stable across 2016–2024, anchored by a fixed paragraph on technical capability and efficient exploration and production. The most visible changes are quantitative (falling countries of operations from 25 to 13 and headcount from 17,800 to 9,800) and the addition of section headers in 2021 ('Who We Are', 'Our History', 'What We Do'). The main framing shift is the 2023 introduction of 'Integrating Sustainability' with 'lasting value for employees, communities and shareholders,' a multi-stakeholder phrasing that is the only substantive values language added, while the core operational message remains unchanged.

Salesforce's About Us page moved from a 2016-2017 framing centred on cloud technology, the 1-1-1 philanthropy model, and growth milestones and awards toward a 2022-2024 framing built on relational language ('bringing people together', 'trust', 'stakeholder capitalism'). Early versions emphasised the company's own pioneering history and 'Ohana' culture; from 2018 onward the page increasingly foregrounded the Fourth Industrial Revolution and customer success. By 2022 the page had shifted to explicit stakeholder-oriented language and a core-values section, with sustainability added as a value in 2023, and by 2024 the text was reduced to stakeholder capitalism and the Pledge 1% movement.

Chevron's About Us language moved from an early focus on 'safe, reliable energy' and 'Human Energy' (2016) and operational values like 'getting results the right way' and 'operating responsibly' (2017-2019), toward a human-progress framing built on 'reliable, affordable and ever-cleaner energy' (2020 onward). From 2020 the copy centers on people, ingenuity and responsibility, and by 2024 it is shorter, with the 'define energy in human terms' headline persisting. Stakeholder, climate or net-zero vocabulary is largely absent across the period; the main shifts are in framing and in the reduction of values and operational language.

The snapshots contain almost only navigation menus and page headers rather than substantive About Us prose, so linguistic analysis of stated values is effectively impossible across 2019-2024. The only visible vocabulary is the tagline 'High Return Organic Growth' in 2019 and 2020, which then disappears, alongside structural menu changes such as the addition of 'Dividend History' from 2023 and 'Report Archives' under Sustainability in 2024. Any conclusions about shifts in stakeholder versus shareholder framing, mission language, or sustainability emphasis cannot be drawn from these captures and would require full page text.

Ford's About Us language moved from a product- and growth-centred narrative in 2016–2018 (quality, safety, green, smart, sustainability metrics, profits and dividends) toward a purpose- and stakeholder-centred framing from 2019 onward ('Freedom of movement drives human progress', 'world's most trusted company'). By 2021 the purpose statement was 'help build a better world, where every person is free to move', with stakeholder and family/shared-ideals language dominating. From 2023–2024 the page condensed into a shorter set of sections (purpose, leadership, history) with stable wording, reflecting a consolidated stakeholder-oriented narrative with the mobility/software pivot stated only briefly.

Alphabet's About Us page moved from a user-centric baseline in 2016 ('Focus on the user and all else will follow', 'Ten things we know to be true') and a 2017 emphasis on machine learning and access, toward a broader social-impact and opportunity framing in 2018-2019 ('expand opportunity for everyone', 'owner's manual for shareholders'). From 2020 the page shrank to a sparse, mission-plus-commitments layout centred on 'Dedicated to improving people's lives' and 'Committed to significantly improving the lives of as many people as possible'. By 2023-2024 the page carried explicit commitments such as 'carbon free by 2030' and 'keeping billions of people safe online', while the core mission statement stayed constant throughout.

Goldman Sachs' About Us language moved from a 2016-2019 navigation-style page centred on people, diversity, awards, and shareholder return, with rotating feature items on Mobileye, Newark revitalization, and colleague headcount. In 2021 the page was reduced to a single descriptive paragraph that frames the firm as an 'investment banking, securities and investment management firm'. By 2024 the text was expanded again, adding an explicit 'Our Purpose and Values' section and broader societal language such as 'broaden individual prosperity' and 'economic progress for all', while retaining the 'people are our greatest asset' statement.

Halliburton's About Us language moved from a short, product-and-services description with community and sustainability framing (2016–2020) to a values-led page built around 'Exceptional experiences require exceptional values' and explicit commitments to diversity, equality and inclusion (2021–2022). By 2023 the opening line added 'advance a sustainable energy future' and the page emphasised innovative technologies, while retaining the core energy-services framing. Across the period the company consistently describes itself as an energy-industry services provider, with stakeholder language (customers, shareholders, global communities) appearing alongside an expanding set of values and sustainability vocabulary. The 2017 snapshot is an error page and was treated as having no usable content.

Home Depot's About Us framing stayed largely fixed from 2016 to 2024, built around 'Built from all the right materials', the 'Inverted Pyramid' ('Put customers and associates first') and the 'Three-legged Stool' of customer and shareholder value. The most consistent changes were updates to store counts and associate headcount, plus the removal of role-based section headings in 2018 and the Canada/Mexico links in 2023. Across the period the text added no stakeholder, sustainability, net zero or AI vocabulary, and it kept the same shareholder-inclusive service language.

IBM's About Us page moved from a 2020 framing centred on 'IBMers believe in progress' and a long historical timeline of inventions (punch cards, Deep Blue, Watson, Summit) toward a more concise, client- and business-outcome framing by 2023-2024. Early snapshots emphasise AI, blockchain, quantum and research heritage, while later versions shift to 'Creators, partners and clients putting technology to work' and then 'help our clients solve their business problems'. The most durable thread is sustainability: the 2021 net-zero goal by 2030 appears from 2023 onward, and the page increasingly features forward-looking AI automation and hybrid cloud language.

Across the snapshots, Intel's public web copy moves from consumer-facing product and device promotion (2016-2018: Core processors, watches, drones, VR, and an early 'artificial intelligence' mention) toward data center, AI and edge framing by 2020-2024 (Xeon Scalable, 'Deep Learning Boost', 'AI Everywhere', 'The AI PC'). The 2022-2023 pages add a brand-level aspirational tone ('Wonderful', 'Era of Intel Evo') and partnership language, while the 2024 page is dominated by product names and AI terminology. The snapshots are fragmentary, mostly navigation and promotional banners rather than a stable 'About Us' text, so stated-values vocabulary such as stakeholders, purpose, or sustainability is largely absent throughout.

J&J's About Us language moved from a 2016 product- and portfolio-centric description (listing rankings across consumer, devices, biologics and pharma) toward a mission- and values-led framing centred on health and the Credo. From 2019 onward the text settled into a long-running 'good health is the foundation' statement emphasizing access, affordability and healthier communities, with stakeholder language appearing mainly in ESG references. The 2024 snapshot shifts to a brand-refresh tone ('health is everything', 'powerful force of care') and deliberately foregrounds the Credo and 'putting people first' while the corporate structure is recast around Innovative Medicine and MedTech.

Across the snapshots, the page moves from a data-driven framing of the JPMorgan Chase Institute as a 'global think tank' (2016-2019), with 'real-time' data, 'shared, global prosperity' and 'smarter decisions', to a shortened 2021-2023 mission centred on 'timely data' and 'prosperity for all', with the founding letters and longer institutional description removed. The 2024 snapshot comes from a different source URL and is a firm-level corporate page emphasising 'Built on Principle', 'integrity, honesty and respect', 'trust and accountability', talent, and diversity and inclusion, so the stated-values emphasis shifts from the Institute's public-good research mission toward the bank's own principles and culture. Note that the 2019 snapshot's copyright line reads 2018, and the 2024 snapshot is not directly comparable in source.

Eli Lilly's About Us language is anchored in its 1876 founding story and a stable set of values (integrity, excellence, respect for people) across 2016-2020. The main structural change was the consolidation of 'promise', 'mission' and 'vision' statements into a single 'Our Purpose' statement from 2019, with the mission and vision wording dropped. Core values were elaborated into longer definitions from 2017, with stakeholder lists (customers, employees, shareholders, partners, suppliers, communities) becoming more explicit over time.

Lowe's About Us language moved from a 2016–2018 navigation-style landing page (corporate citizenship, investors, careers, sponsorships) with no substantive mission text, through a 2019 legal disclaimer, to a 2020 onward 'More Than Home Improvement' customer-and-associate-centred narrative. From 2020 the framing centres on mission, strategy pillars, and an omni-channel retail experience. In 2022 the stated strategy shifted from four pillars to the 'Total Home Strategy' with five focus areas (Pro, Online, Installation Services, Localization, Assortment), which persisted into 2024. Stated metrics were refreshed each year, and the 2024 edition drops the 'in the United States and Canada' qualifier and the community investment figure while adding 'omnichannel' spelling and 'deliver' without 'we'.

McDonald's About Us page remained structurally stable across 2016–2024, anchored by the Ray Kroc founding narrative and the unchanged claim of 36,000+ restaurants in 100+ countries. Framing stayed brand-history and navigation-oriented throughout, with no explicit shareholder or stakeholder vocabulary such as purpose, sustainability, or net zero appearing in the text. The main changes were incremental: a 2018 intro sentence about values and leadership, periodic reshuffling of link tiles, the 2020 addition of a recalls section, and in 2024 a new 'Meet the 1 in 8' and 'Where you start stays with you' tile, which is the only new consumer-oriented language. Overall the page's stated values emphasis stayed minimal, centred on 'Values in Action' as a community-leadership link rather than a developed value statement.

Medtronic's 2016 About Us page was marketing-led, featuring value-based healthcare, partnership and patient stories rather than a formal mission statement. From 2017 onward the page centres on the 1960 Mission statement, which frames the company around human welfare, biomedical engineering, quality, fair profit and employees, with citizenship as a final commitment. Over time the text was trimmed: the citizenship item and the foundation/volunteer call-to-action were dropped after 2021, and the 2022 onward versions keep only five commitments with a 60th-anniversary framing, so the stated values have become more concise and more consistently mission-oriented.

The snapshots are Facebook page scrapes rather than genuine About Us text, so the language reflects page chrome, navigation and occasional community posts rather than stated corporate values. Early years (2017-2019) show UI navigation and community-oriented posts such as 'Hope brings us together', while 2020-2024 snapshots are dominated by login walls, navigation menus and footer links. The only trajectory visible is a shift from community/hope framing toward corporate product-family listings (Meta Pay, Meta Quest, Threads) and a 2021 rebrand to 'Meta' in the footer, with no substantive values language in any year.

Marathon Petroleum's About page moved from a fact-heavy 2016–2018 profile of refining capacity, network counts and pipeline miles toward a corporate-values narrative from 2019 onward. The 2019–2020 versions introduce "corporate citizenship" and an explicit stakeholder list alongside values such as health and safety, diversity and inclusion. From 2021 the framing is recast as "creating shared value" with a stakeholder list that adds governments and shareholders, and the core values are reworded to emphasize inclusion and collaboration. From 2022 to 2024 the text is largely static, with only a shortened refinery description and the MPLX relationship restated.

Merck's About Us language moved from a product-inclusive mission in 2016 (medicines, vaccines, biologic therapies, consumer care, animal health, with an aspiration to be 'the best healthcare company in the world') to a narrower 'research-intensive biopharmaceutical' framing from 2017. Values and ethics language was added in 2018 and held steady through 2020. The 2021 rewrite introduced 'invent for a more hopeful future' and a broader corporate-responsibility framing, and 2022 added an explicit 'Our purpose' statement with 'diverse and inclusive' and 'sustainable' wording, which was unchanged in 2023. The 2024 snapshot is unreadable binary data, so the trajectory after 2023 cannot be assessed.

Morgan Stanley's About Us page moved from a long, chronological corporate history (2016–2020) that emphasized market milestones, global office expansion and community giving, to a short, present-tense sustainability and inclusion page (2021–2024) built around impact metrics, the Institute for Sustainable Investing and diversity language. The 2016–2020 snapshots were identical, so the real change was an abrupt replacement in 2021 rather than gradual drift. From 2021 onward the wording was stable, with only the country count changing in 2024.

Microsoft's About Us page moved from a 2016 framing built around a corporate mission and strategy ('mobile-first, cloud-first world', 'intelligent cloud platform') with extensive corporate, legal, and investor navigation, to a leaner, more values-oriented presentation from 2017 onward. The mission statement stayed substantively constant, though its wording shifted from 'Empower every person and every organization' to 'Empowering others' with a shortened mission line from 2020. Over time, sustainability and AI became the most prominent featured themes, with 'carbon negative by 2030' and 'Microsoft AI' appearing as headline programs, while the page's language moved toward social responsibility and 'force for good' framing by 2020 and remained stable through 2024.

Nike's About Us language moved from a product- and innovation-centred framing in 2016–2018 ('culture of invention', 'Sustainable innovation is a catalyst') toward a mission-led, explicitly purpose-driven framing from 2019 ('Our mission is what drives us', 'expand human potential') that places diversity, community impact and sustainability alongside innovation. From 2019 onward the text is largely stable, with the main later change being the 2019 sustainability mission ('double our business, while cutting our environmental impact in half') being replaced in 2020 by the more aspirational 'Protecting the Future of Sport' and a 'fair, sustainable future' vision, and the removal of 'Hurley' from the brand list in 2021.

NVIDIA's About Us framing moved from a product-and-history narrative in 2017 (GPU invention, PC gaming, 'the AI computing company') to a 2018-2022 period in which the page was reduced to a single unchanged paragraph about GPU deep learning and AI. The 2023 snapshot expanded into a long, use-case-driven page built around 'AI and the metaverse,' 'Engine of AI,' and autonomous machines, with heavy emphasis on customers and applications. The 2024 version returned to a shorter structure, shifting the headline emphasis from metaverse to 'AI and digital twins,' adding generative AI and explicit sustainability language ('net zero'), while retaining the culture statement 'Like No Place You've Ever Worked.' Overall, the trajectory is from a company describing its heritage in graphics to one describing itself as an AI infrastructure provider with growing attention to industry impact and sustainability.

Oracle's About Us page moved from a broad corporate-information hub in 2016, with governance, customer, partner and career language, to a short, metric-driven page in 2017-2019 centred on customers, cloud services and autonomous technology. From 2020 the page is dominated by a company-history timeline and a 'Socially Responsible' / 'Diverse and Inclusive' tagline, and by 2022-2023 it is mostly a set of links and timeline entries. Across the period, stakeholder language around inclusion and sustainability grew while the page's own descriptive content thinned.

Occidental's About Us page moved from a detailed, business-segment-led description (upstream, midstream and marketing, OxyChem, 'Partner of Choice') in 2016-2019 to a shorter, more aspirational framing from 2020 onward. From 2020 the emphasis shifts to lower-carbon futures, carbon management and Oxy Low Carbon Ventures, and by 2022 the page adopts a mission-and-values structure with 'net zero' and 'reducing greenhouse gas emissions' language. The 2022-2024 pages are nearly identical, with only the regional list changing in 2024 when Latin America drops from the 'What We Do' teams sentence.

Pfizer's About Us language moved from a 2016-2017 framing centred on products, pipeline, shareholders and a broad 'Working Together for a Healthier World' mission, toward a purpose-led stance from 2018 onward built on 'Health for All' and 'Breakthroughs that change patients' lives'. Stakeholder and access themes (equity, social justice, community investment) gained prominence in 2021, and by 2023-2024 the page had expanded into a large navigational timeline and corporate-responsibility index with COVID-19, mRNA and misinformation content. Shareholder-facing language persisted throughout but became secondary to patient-centred purpose.

Phillips 66's About Us language moved from a 2016 baseline of financial and operational detail (dividends, shareholder return, debt reduction, growth capital) toward a values-led, 'Providing Energy. Improving Lives.' framing from 2017 onward, with shareholder-value language persisting through 2022. From 2022 the page increasingly emphasizes 'Our Energy', sustainable communities and innovation, and by 2023-2024 it has shifted to a short, values-first summary built around renewable fuels, batteries, carbon capture, hydrogen, community and social impact. Across the period the text grew substantially shorter in its financial content while adding alternative-energy vocabulary.

Starbucks' About Us language was stable from 2016 through 2021, centred on a customer-connection narrative with 'a connection' and 'a little better than we found it' framing. In 2022 the page was restructured into a heritage-driven story with sections on Our Heritage, Coffee & Craft, Our Partners and a purpose statement, adding explicit stakeholder language about partners, belonging and communities and a 'purpose goes far beyond profit' claim. The 2024 update changed only the mission wording, moving from 'inspire and nurture the human spirit' to 'nurture the limitless possibilities of human connection', otherwise retaining the 2022-2023 structure.

Schwab's About Us language moved from a 2016-2017 framing centered on the 'power of investing,' client assets, and awards (Human Rights Campaign equality ratings, FORTUNE, J.D. Power) toward a 2020-2022 emphasis on a 'better, more modern way to build and manage wealth' and 'serve you,' with growing stats on client assets and accounts after the TD Ameritrade combination. By 2023-2024 the copy shifted to 'One combined company dedicated to serving investors' and self-described 'champions of investors,' with values language (purpose, optimism, 'Main Street,' 'human approach,' 'authentic and full selves') and a reduced reliance on awards. Across the period, the text moved from a corporate-governance and awards-driven profile to a more client-purpose and community-oriented narrative.

SLB's About Us language moved from a 2016-2019 baseline of 'world's leading provider of technology for reservoir characterization, drilling, production, and processing to the oil and gas industry' with product-and-service framing, stewardship language, and 'Driven to create value for our customers, our shareholders and our employees' to a 2020-2021 'technology innovator' and 'common sense of purpose' framing centered on energy access and society's progress. From 2022 onward the text adopts explicit purpose statements ('Our purpose'), customer-centric and partnership language, and energy-transition and net-zero vocabulary, culminating in 2023 and 2024 with decarbonization, net-zero targets and a 'lower-carbon world'. Across the period, headcount and nationality figures were updated, and the text shifted from an oil-and-gas-industry identity toward an energy-transition identity, though it retains hydrocarbon-recovery references.

Target's About Us page moved from a narrow, design-led brand story (2016–2019, centred on 'a mind for design, a passion for innovation' and product quality) to a metrics-heavy corporate profile (2020–2022) built around store counts, revenue, distribution centers and owned brands, with 'purpose' surfacing as a link label. By 2024 the page was reframed around family and everyday life ('help all families discover the joy of everyday life'), with a navigation-style layout and expanded footprint and team statistics, and it no longer carries the 2016–2019 design narrative. Across the period the language shifts from product and design emphasis toward scale, operational footprint and a consumer-family positioning, while the 5% profit-to-communities figure is the one stable commitment throughout.

TJX's About Us language moves from a detailed, store- and sourcing-heavy description of its off-price model (2016-2017) toward a shorter, more mission-focused presentation. Early versions emphasize 'treasure-hunt' shopping, flexibility and historical growth, while later versions trim operational detail and retain the same core mission and flexibility claims. The 2022-2024 pages add explicit references to pandemic recovery, career opportunities and corporate responsibility, but the stakeholder language remains limited and capital return to shareholders is consistently emphasized.

Thermo Fisher's About Us language moves from a CSR-report and product-and-acquisition framing in 2016-2017 toward a stable mission statement ('enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer') from 2018 onward. Descriptive copy about revenue, employees and brands is dropped after 2018, and the 2020-2021 pages foreground responsibility to 'the global community'. By 2023-2024 the page is dominated by customer-story and 'Going a step beyond means...' framing, with added themes of diversity, equity and environmental goals, while the mission wording itself stays essentially constant.

Tesla's About Us language moved from a long, product-centric narrative in 2016 (Roadster, Model S, Model X, Gigafactory specifics, 'cars without compromise') toward a sustainability-mission framing by 2018 that emphasizes clean energy ecosystems and fossil-fuel reduction. From 2019 to 2022 the text stayed largely stable, adding Semi, Model Y and Cybertruck and Gigafactory Shanghai. In 2023 and 2024 the page was abruptly condensed into a short, aspirational statement centered on 'The Future is Sustainable', scale, vertical integration and first-principles engineering, dropping the earlier product histories.

UNH's About Us language moved from a 2016 product- and innovation-led framing ('most diversified health care company', 'innovative approaches, products and services') toward a 2017-2020 'health and well-being company' identity built on technology, data and scale metrics. From 2021 onward the page shifted to mission and people language ('Our Mission & Values', 'Health Equity', 'Corporate Governance'), then 2022-2024 emphasised sustainability, equity, and a mission-driven 'more sustainable path forward' while still explicitly naming shareholders alongside consumers and care providers. Quantitative 'by the numbers' claims were largely replaced by people and workforce framing in 2023, and the 2024 text leans on sustainability and mission rather than innovation.

Valero's About Us language moved from a detailed, data-heavy description of a fuels, petrochemicals and power manufacturer (2016-2019, with asset counts, capacity and outlet figures) to a short values-and-brand page from 2020 onward built around 'Guiding Principles', 'Leadership' and 'Advancing the Future of Energy'. The 2020-2024 text is largely stable, with the main changes being the ethanol plant count, the addition of Diamond Green Diesel and renewable diesel references, and a growing list of conduct and supplier links. Stakeholder-style language appears mainly in the later 'Community', 'Governance' and 'sustainable energy' wording, while the 2016-2019 text stayed product- and asset-centric.

Across 2016 to 2024 the Wells Fargo About page moved from a vision-and-values framing with strong community, homeownership and environment language toward thinner, more generic navigation copy. The 2016 to 2018 snapshots centre on 'Vision and Values', 'stronger communities' and lending volume claims, while 2019 introduces Spanish-language content that reframes the vision as 'ayudar a nuestros clientes a alcanzar el éxito financiero'. By 2020 to 2024 the page is largely reduced to link labels and a 'Learn about our commitment to helping people and communities succeed financially' line, with the 'Vision and Values' wording no longer appearing in the English text.

ExxonMobil's About Us framing stays anchored in a product-and-operations narrative ('Fueling the world safely and responsibly') across the period, with the core introductory paragraph unchanged from 2019 to 2021. The 2023 snapshot adds explicit 'next-generation technologies' and 'growing needs' language and expands the brand list to include chemicals, while the 2024 version shifts most decisively toward energy-transition and lower-emissions vocabulary, reframing the company as balancing supply with 'lower-emission solutions'. Throughout, the language remains focused on energy supply and the company's own competitive position rather than broader stakeholder commitments.
